correctness.rationale: Lucas applied to each binomial and independent summation of its digit cubes give character weights (1,-1,0,1,1). To check the limit and spectrum independently, first restrict both n and n+h to the block. The exact Laurent polynomial for those correlations is the product for i=0,...,r-1 of (4-z^(2*5^i)-z^(-2*5^i)+z^(4*5^i)+z^(-4*5^i)). The unwrapped sum differs by at most h terms, so this gives the same normalized fixed-h limit. The exponent h is impossible if h is odd. For even h the unique balanced-quinary representation of h/2 uses digits 0, +/-1, +/-2; the value after normalization is 4^(-j) times (-1) to the number of digits +/-1, with j the number of nonzero digits. For 0<=h<5^r the balanced representations are exactly the nonnegative half of the r-digit balanced words. At each selected nonzero position two choices are positive and two negative; reflection preserves sign and halves each nonzero class. This yields the displayed signed counts and the only positive shifts of magnitude 1/4 are 2*5^i and 4*5^i with the stated signs. For the stronger exact remainder claim, splitting the unwrapped sum by n mod 5 gives the single surviving coefficient 4,+1,-1,-1,+1 and predecessor q,q+1,q,q+1,q respectively. Shifts 0 and 1 have exact values 4^r and -1; all other predecessors decrease, proving eventual constant integer remainder by induction. This also confirms the four small-shift identities. The frozen scope is fixed h, not a uniform asymptotic for growing shifts.
correctness.reproduction: Independent standard-library recomputation, no source script executed: start Pascal row [1], replace it with [1]+[(a+b)%5 for adjacent row entries a,b]+[1] each step; map sum(cube(entry)) mod 5 to 0,1,-1,-1,1 for n=0,...,3749. Compare to the digit-product sequence (construct successive blocks by multiplying the previous whole block by each of the five weights). For h=0,...,624 take the direct unwrapped dot products S4,S5 from the Pascal sequence and S6 from the checked digit-product rule. Use C=(S5-S4)/(3*4^4), b=S4-4^4*C, and check b integral, S6=4^6*C+b, sharp equality classes and full histograms on each prefix of length 5^r for r=1,...,4. All passed. At r=4 the zero count was 312; the counts per sign at j=1,2,3,4 were 4,24,64,64. These finite computations supplement the proof. Frozen checker inspected as source only.

value.rationale: The usual correlation normalization loses all information on this sparse support. The natural active normalization yields a complete exact two-point statistic: precisely the odd shifts vanish, the signs balance at each nontrivial magnitude and the strongest lags have a sharp arithmetic classification. This is an all-depth benchmark for sparse digit-defined correlations rather than a recomputation of a Franel residue table.
